identity.title: Breast cancer cellular and gene-based therapies: Current approaches, clinical results, and future perspectives.

content.abstract: Cellular and gene-based therapies are being investigated as potential strategies to address current treatment limitations in breast cancer. Adoptive cell therapies, such as CAR-T, TCR-T, TILs and NK cell-based therapies, are currently under investigation for their ability to selectively target tumor-associated antigens. Also, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing is being investigated as a strategy to enhance T cell persistence, improve tumor infiltration, and increase resistance to immunosuppressive signaling. Although cellular and gene-based therapies have transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies, their application in breast cancer remains limited by antigen heterogeneity, immune exclusion, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Among current approaches, TIL-based therapies have provided some of the clearest evidence of clinical activity selected patients, whereas the clinical efficacy of CAR-T and gene-editing strategies as standalone interventions remains uncertain. Future progress may depend on biomarker-guided, combinatorial approaches rather than single-modality therapies. This review examines the current applications, clinical evidence, and limitations of these approaches in breast cancer.
